guide.electron.title: Electron · Engineering Handbook
guide.electron.first_light.title: Your first light
guide.electron.first_light.subtitle: 01 / A closed loop
guide.electron.first_light.p0: Place a hand-crank supply, 220 ohm resistor and LED on top of a smooth-stone bench. Face the terminals upward for your first circuit.
guide.electron.first_light.p1: Use the spool to connect supply + to resistor A, resistor B to LED +, and LED minus back to supply minus.
guide.electron.first_light.p2: Use the supply with an empty hand. One crank per second adds 5 J, up to 200 J. Reversed LEDs and circuits without a return wire do not light.
guide.electron.first_light.p3: The supply produces 5 V with internal resistance. Connecting an LED directly causes overcurrent and eventually destroys it.
guide.electron.wiring.title: Several wires in one block
guide.electron.wiring.subtitle: 02 / Straight first + automatic routing
guide.electron.wiring.p0: A spool starts with 16 blocks of wire. Click a pin or surface to select a start, then any target to connect. A new surface node costs 1/16 block. Aligned points use a straight run; diagonal targets and obstacles use routing.
guide.electron.wiring.p1: Place intermediate nodes to choose where a route passes. Aim to preview, then click to connect. A component pin ends the chain; clicking the current node also finishes. Failed connections consume nothing and leave no partial tap.
guide.electron.wiring.p2: Click any existing wire midway to make a branch. Its color and total paid length are preserved. Different colors can join explicitly; simply crossing does not short them.
guide.electron.wiring.p3: Wire follows exposed corners and steps, up to 32 blocks per run. Components can sit on a bench. Only power cable can span complete tower terminals, up to 64 blocks; walls require ports.
guide.electron.wall_ports.title: Through a solid wall
guide.electron.wall_ports.subtitle: 03 / Two-core wall ports
guide.electron.wall_ports.p0: Use a wall port on any face of an ordinary solid block. The wall remains intact and two independent contacts appear on the opposite face.
guide.electron.wall_ports.p1: Copper is core 0 and silver is core 1. Both sides connect 0 to 0 and 1 to 1. Use one for supply and one for return; they are separate conductors.
guide.electron.wall_ports.p2: A wall block has four mounting corners. Overlapping cores are refused. Thick walls need a port in each block; aligned adjacent contacts join matching cores.
guide.electron.wall_ports.p3: Containers, machines and bedrock cannot be drilled. Removing the wall disconnects and recovers attachments. Blocks carrying wiring or ports cannot currently be pushed by pistons.
guide.electron.measurement.title: Multimeter and measurement HUD
guide.electron.measurement.subtitle: Live readings in survival require an instrument
guide.electron.measurement.p0: 1  Tooltips retain rated specifications and wiring instructions. In survival, holding or using a device does not reveal live voltage, current, resistance or stored energy; battery items also hide their live charge bar. Creative mode permits diagnostic readings. Light, motion and battery panel indicators remain visible physical states.
guide.electron.measurement.p1: 2  Hold the multimeter and select two terminals: COM first, then the probe. The bottom-right HUD continuously shows their voltage difference. Sneak-use a device to read its current and state, or a wire to read branch current. Putting the meter away hides the HUD.
guide.electron.measurement.p2: 3  Use in air to clear probes; sneak-use in air toggles V / Ω. Resistance mode measures the equivalent resistance between the probes, including parallel paths. Powered sources or charged capacitors block resistance measurement. Disconnect and discharge first; open circuits and out-of-range values show OL.
guide.electron.measurement.p3: 4  The server calculates readings and sends them only to the player holding the meter, with regular refreshes. Unavailable, unloaded or paused targets do not retain stale values. Voltage probes need a common circuit reference. A device voltage rating is not a live measurement.
guide.electron.logic.title: Two logic gate families
guide.electron.logic.subtitle: 05 / Redstone and electrical wiring
guide.electron.logic.p0: Redstone models have red boards and redstone contacts. Eight gate functions and the binary memory keep vanilla redstone interfaces. The arrow marks the output.
guide.electron.logic.p1: Electrical models have green panels and five terminals. VCC takes 5 V and GND the return. A/B are inputs; Y is the output. NOT and BUFFER do not use B.
guide.electron.logic.p2: Electrical gates need power. Input at or below 30% of supply is 0 and at or above 70% is 1. Intermediate or floating input is X. No power gives Z; neither X nor Z is a valid 0.
guide.electron.logic.p3: Electrical gates have a two-tick delay, input impedance, idle consumption and limited output current. Do not drive motors directly or short the output to a supply rail.
guide.electron.crafting.title: Materials and crafting
guide.electron.crafting.subtitle: 06 / Starter workshop
guide.electron.crafting.p0: The starter recipes use a vanilla crafting table or the assembly table 3x3 grid. The main mod does not require the calculator generator.
guide.electron.crafting.p1: Spool: two copper, two paper, a stick and two planks. Hand-crank supply: two copper, two iron, redstone and a lever.
guide.electron.crafting.p2: Resistors: two copper and two bricks, with coal for 100 ohm, charcoal for 220 ohm or quartz for 1 kilohm. LED: two copper, redstone, glass and red dye.
guide.electron.crafting.p3: Wrench: two iron, copper and a stick. Use to rotate 90 degrees; sneak-use rotates back. Disconnect first. Floor/ceiling components orient to the player; wall text starts upright.
guide.electron.protection.title: Protection before power
guide.electron.protection.subtitle: 07 / Diode and fuse
guide.electron.protection.p0: Put a 25 mA fuse in series with the supply. Accumulated overload blows it. It acts before the LED burns in the tested direct-supply circuit, but is not a substitute for a current-limiting resistor.
guide.electron.protection.p1: The silicon diode conducts from A to K; the silver band marks K. Its forward drop is about 0.7 V and its rated forward current is 50 mA. Reverse connection blocks current.
guide.electron.protection.p2: Fuse: one copper, iron nugget and glass, producing two. Diode: two copper, quartz and redstone. Damaged parts become scrap; check the fault before replacing.
guide.electron.protection.p3: Overload produces arcs and smoke. Severe overcurrent produces local popping particles and sound. Failed low-voltage components open the circuit without destroying nearby buildings.
guide.electron.precision.title: Crossings and precise connections
guide.electron.precision.subtitle: 08 / Bridges + magnifying visor
guide.electron.precision.p0: Install a bridge on the crossing face. L0 traces rise over existing conductors; for continuous upper-layer wiring, select L1 and bridge every supporting face. Routing avoids corner foot clearance and nodes cannot be placed there. Move existing corner connections before installing a bridge.
guide.electron.precision.p1: Ceramic feet replace the decorative parallel rails; colored runs are actual wires. Layers remain isolated unless you explicitly tap a wire. Saved bridge routes retain materials and connections. Sneak-use cutters to remove a bridge; unsupported runs return their paid wire length.
guide.electron.precision.p2: Visor recipe: two glass, copper, iron and leather. Use to equip, or put it in the head slot. Hold magnify (default Z) for 3x; sneaking gives 6x. The key can be changed in Controls.
guide.electron.precision.p3: Magnification slows aiming to help select fine wires. Release the key to return immediately. It is disabled in screens and does not blur the handbook.
guide.electron.scales.title: Three scales, shared electricity
guide.electron.scales.subtitle: 09 / Scale and ratings
guide.electron.scales.p0: Large circuits use cable and enclosure blocks such as distribution boxes, breakers, lamps and motors. Small circuits still use one device per block with fine wire. Both share the electrical network while retaining their wire sizes, ratings and models.
guide.electron.scales.p1: MOSFETs and relays let small control circuits switch power loads. DC converters change voltage according to input power and efficiency. Redstone cannot convert to or from electricity; an electrically actuated contact only blocks or passes existing redstone.
guide.electron.scales.p2: Integrated circuits are planned as small item parts placed, traced and soldered on player-designed PCBs. Resistors and logic ICs will not occupy individual world blocks. This system is not yet available.
guide.electron.scales.p3: Tooltips show the current model ratings. LEDs recommend 5–20 mA, corresponding to about 2.1–2.4 V forward drop. Use a 220 ohm series resistor with 5 V; a forward drop is not a direct supply rating.

guide.electron.series_parallel.title: Series, parallel and mixed circuits
guide.electron.series_parallel.subtitle: Wiring determines voltage and current; no mode selection
guide.electron.series_parallel.p0: Series: supply + → R1 → R2 → supply − forms one path. Both resistors carry the same current; resistance adds and voltage divides in proportion to resistance. Opening any point interrupts the loop.
guide.electron.series_parallel.p1: Parallel: connect both ends of R1 and R2 to the same pair of junctions. Branch voltages are nearly equal (wires have small resistance); each draws I = V/R, and branch currents add. Sharing only one end is not parallel.
guide.electron.series_parallel.p2: Tap an existing wire with the spool to make a branch. Crossing alone does not join wires; bridge layers remain isolated. Give each parallel LED branch its own series resistor. Opening one branch leaves the other working.
guide.electron.series_parallel.p3: For a mixed circuit, add a common series resistor ahead of parallel branches. Sneak-click a device with the meter for current; probe two terminals for voltage. The crank has 5 ohm internal resistance and wires drop voltage, so loaded voltage is below nominal 5 V.
guide.electron.timing.title: Button, capacitor and a fading LED
guide.electron.timing.subtitle: Stored energy and per-tick simulation; 20 ticks at normal speed
guide.electron.timing.p0: The momentary button is normally open. Right click with an empty hand to close it for 20 ticks, then reopen. Repeated clicks during a pulse do not extend it. It is a non-polar contact, not a voltage source or redstone output.
guide.electron.timing.p1: Fading lamp: crank + → button A; button B → capacitor +; capacitor − → supply −. Branch capacitor + through 220 ohm to LED +; LED − returns to capacitor −. Crank for energy, then press once. After release, the capacitor supplies the LED, which gradually dims.
guide.electron.timing.p2: The polarized capacitor is 100 mF (0.1 F), rated 10 V, with 1 ohm ESR and 1 Mohm leakage; its light stripe marks negative. Charging, discharging and reverse current are simulated. Sustained reversal, overvoltage or overcurrent damages it; failed capacitors are high impedance and store no energy.
guide.electron.timing.p3: Sneak-click with the meter for internal voltage and joules; positive current charges, negative current discharges. Saves retain voltage; unloaded or paused networks do not advance. Removed items are discharged. A 10k resistor pulls a logic input to VCC or GND; a button to the opposite rail prevents floating input after release.

guide.electron.power_modules.title: Energy storage and branching
guide.electron.power_modules.subtitle: Four battery pins · Two separate bus rails
guide.electron.power_modules.p0: 1  Batteries are crafted empty. Wire crank +/− to IN+/IN− to charge, and OUT+/OUT− to a complete load circuit. Recommended charging is 5 V, max 6 V / 250 mA. Output is 5 V with 5 Ω internal resistance and a 100 mA limit. Shorts collapse voltage and consume stored energy.
guide.electron.power_modules.p1: 2  Capacity is 200 J. The battery stores 80%% of actual input power; discharge efficiency is 90%%. Returns share a ground, so charging and output can work together. Backfeeding OUT does not charge it; looping output into input loses energy. Sneak-use with an empty hand toggles output only.
guide.electron.power_modules.p2: 3  Five panel lights show approximate charge. Use the multimeter for precise energy, output and charge readings. Survival inventory hides the live charge bar; creative mode may show it. Charge survives normal removal and replacement; modules do not stack. Paused or unloaded networks freeze. Sustained reverse polarity or overvoltage damages the module, leaving scrap.
guide.electron.power_modules.p3: 4  A1–A4 form one strip bus and B1–B4 another, isolated from each other. Adjacent same-bus pins have 0.002 Ω resistance. Use A as supply and B as return, with each parallel load connected across both. Each LED branch still needs its own series resistor.
guide.electron.redstone_switch.title: Electrically actuated redstone switch
guide.electron.redstone_switch.subtitle: Electricity moves the contact · Redstone stays redstone
guide.electron.redstone_switch.p0: 1  Electricity and redstone are independent systems; neither powers or converts into the other. This device only lets an electric circuit open or close a redstone path. Its electrical pins are a polarized +/− coil. The redstone path enters at the panel arrow tail and leaves at its tip, with no electrical pins.
guide.electron.redstone_switch.p1: 2  Supply the coil with 5 V, max 6 V; its resistance is 1 kΩ. It closes at 3.5 V and releases at 1.5 V with a 2-game-tick mechanical delay. Connect supply, electric switch and coil into a complete loop. The moving contact has an animation and sound.
guide.electron.redstone_switch.p2: 3  Feed an existing vanilla redstone signal into the arrow tail; connect redstone wiring or a redstone lamp to the tip. Closed contacts pass the original strength 0–15 unchanged; open contacts output 0. Electricity without redstone input always outputs 0, and redstone cannot supply electric wires.
guide.electron.redstone_switch.p3: 4  Mounting face and rotation determine input and output direction; redstone emits only from the arrow side. Loss of power releases the coil; network pauses or damage open contacts immediately. Sustained reverse polarity or overvoltage burns the device. Redstone gates still use redstone; wire gates still use electricity.

guide.electron.control.title: MOSFET and relay load control
guide.electron.control.subtitle: Small control circuits drive power loads
guide.electron.control.p0: 1  The N-channel MOSFET switches the low side: supply + → load → D, S → supply −. Connect the control signal to G and share its return with S. It switches on at 3 V gate-source and off at 1.5 V; gate-source max ±12 V, drain-source max 30 V / 2 A.
guide.electron.control.p1: 2  G has a 1 MΩ discharge path to S, with 0.08 Ω on resistance between D/S and a body diode from S to D. A wire logic gate Y can drive G without carrying the load current. Reversed wiring or excessive ratings can damage it.
guide.electron.control.p2: 3  Wire relay COIL+/− to a 5 V control circuit and COM/NO in series with the load. Coil and contacts are electrically isolated, so the load may use another supply. Pull-in is 3.5 V, release 1.5 V, with 2 ticks delay; contacts max 30 V / 2 A. This relay switches electricity only.
guide.electron.control.p3: 4  Motors model armature resistance, back EMF, inertia and shaft load. Use to select free, loaded or locked shaft; locking increases current. Add a breaker, use cable for the power loop and watch startup or stall with the meter. This release simulates shaft loads; it does not yet drive external pumps or conveyors.
guide.electron.conversion.title: DC step-up and step-down
guide.electron.conversion.subtitle: Voltage changes; input power still limits output
guide.electron.conversion.p0: 1  Small circuits use five fixed-output modules. Buck outputs 3.3 / 5 / 12 V accept 4.5–30 / 7–30 / 14–30 V respectively. Boost outputs 12 / 24 V accept 2.5–10 / 2.5–20 V. Each model accepts an input range; individual input/output pairs are not separate devices.
guide.electron.conversion.p1: 2  Fixed models have no voltage-setting interface. Craft and replace the module to change its nominal output; sneak-use only toggles output. The future PCB stage will combine small power ICs, inductors, capacitors and feedback resistors by soldering. Adjustable ICs will derive their setting from feedback parts, not a free voltage entry.
guide.electron.conversion.p2: 3  This averaged model has 85%% efficiency and a 0.5 J buffer. Input limits are 300 mA for boost and 500 mA for buck; output is at most 500 mA and is further limited by actual input power. Undervoltage stops charging; overvoltage or reverse polarity may damage it. Inadequate power causes droop or pulsing. Measure actual output with the meter.
guide.electron.conversion.p3: 4  Sustained reverse polarity, excessive input voltage or overvoltage forced into the output damages the converter. Removal discharges its small buffer; world saves preserve it and pauses/unloading freeze it. Redstone remains independent and cannot replace an electrical supply.
guide.electron.distribution.title: Low-voltage distribution
guide.electron.distribution.subtitle: Cable, branching, protection and loads
guide.electron.distribution.p0: 1  Craft the 24 V hand-crank DC generator. One crank per second adds 50 J; capacity is 2000 J with 4 Ω internal resistance and a 2 A output limit. Power devices have separate enclosure models and a creative tab. They connect to small devices through actual electrical terminals.
guide.electron.distribution.p1: 2  Single-core cable has 0.002 Ω per block and a 5 A rating; lay supply and return separately. Fine wire has 0.02 Ω per block and a 250 mA rating; sustained overload burns it. Color only labels a wire. The 128-run world limit is removed; 32-block runs and the 256-node per-network solver budget remain.
guide.electron.distribution.p2: 3  Connect supply + → 1 A breaker → box bus A; supply − → bus B. A/B are isolated, with four terminals per rail for branches. The engineering lamp is a 24 V / 2.4 W load whose brightness follows power. Connect the motor on another branch and control it with a MOSFET or relay.
guide.electron.distribution.p3: Stack at least 3 steel tower sections on a solid foundation, then place an upward-facing tower terminal. Use an L0 cable spool on both towers. A1–A4 share one bus; B1–B4 share another. Run supply and return separately; sag consumes real cable length.

guide.electron.power_grid.title: Power grids and plants
guide.electron.power_grid.subtitle: 240 V rectified bus > 24 V loads > 5 V control
guide.electron.power_grid.p0: Build the structure first, with the controller facing up. Tooltips list foundations, casings and environmental checks. Thermal uses coal; nuclear uses fuel rods; hydro needs a two-block head; wind needs a clear rotor and tower; collectors need actual lightning.
guide.electron.power_grid.p1: Route generator +/− through separate power cables to tower A/B rails, then the receiving service IN. Service OUT feeds station IN; station OUT supplies 24 V loads. The service inlet creates no energy. The station runs at 92% efficiency.
guide.electron.power_grid.p2: Aerial cables cost their curved length. A 240 V span with less than two blocks of ground/obstacle clearance leaks current, arcs and hurts entities near the arc. Raise the towers and keep cables clear of buildings.
guide.electron.power_grid.p3: Use the multimeter for live readings. Nuclear generation stops without coolant and a hot reactor shuts down. This is an energy-accounted rectified DC model, without AC phases, radiation or fuel reprocessing.
guide.electron.mechanics.title: Motors, shafts and platforms
guide.electron.mechanics.subtitle: Connect along the central output axis
guide.electron.mechanics.p0: The motor face has a central output shaft. Place aligned shafts and a rotating platform along it. All three axes work; straight transmissions scan up to 16 blocks.
guide.electron.mechanics.p1: Use a plain block on the platform to mount one item. Sneak-use with an empty hand to retrieve it. Breaking the platform returns the mounted item. Containers and data-bearing items are rejected.
guide.electron.mechanics.p2: A mounted block adds motor load. Breaking the shaft or stopping the motor stops the platform. The mounted item is a rotating display; it does not execute world-block behavior or move players.
guide.electron.mechanics.p3: Each conductor color is a separate item. Using a spool in air ends the run instead of changing color. Lamps need actual power, and shaders need the appropriate light mapping or emissive materials; unpowered states stay dark.
